newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK December inflation data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK December inflation data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK inflation data which showed the headline rate at 2.5 pct in December vs expected 2.6 pct and the underlying rate at 3.1 percent as expected.
"On the better side of market expectations, a reassuring figure. The headline rate and core rate look quite good so the market should be relieved from these sorts of figures."
"The key UK RPI was at the lower end of expectations and as such provided the Chancellor with all the ammunition he needed to justify a steady rate policy if he wants.

"The breakdown of the index is mixed with some categories showing a modest acceleration such as household services...but others a slight decline such as leisure goods and clothing and footwear. Following two successive large monthly gains, weakness last month (in clothing and footwear) will be seen offering new evidence that competitiveness factors continue to limit retailers' ability to insitgate sustainable price hikes."

"It's a bit better than the market thought but not particularly surprising given what's happening to PPI and sterling. Inflation is moderating, it's coming down. I think it's going to be less than 2.5 percent by the late spring and less than 2.0 percent by the end of the year."
